children: Eikon Therapeutics reported a third-quarter 2026 net loss attributable to common stockholders of $86.1 million, compared with $71.1 million a year earlier. The company ended September with $461.7 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, and expects its funds to support operations into the first quarter of 2028. It also reported clinical progress across its oncology pipeline, including enrollment in a registrational NSCLC trial and an IND submission for a prostate cancer candidate.
Research and development expenses were $71.8 million for the quarter, up from $59.3 million in the third quarter of 2025.
General and administrative expenses were $18.7 million, compared with $15.4 million a year earlier; total operating expenses were $90.6 million, up from $74.8 million.
Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $86.1 million, or $1.59 per share, compared with $71.1 million, or $24.24 per share, in the prior-year quarter.
Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $461.7 million at September 30, 2026. Net cash used in operating activities was $224.0 million for the nine months ended September 30.

At the 2026 ESMO Congress, Eikon presented updated TeLuRide-005 results for EIK1001 with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy in NSCLC. In the pooled efficacy-evaluable population, the objective response rate was 63.1%; the squamous cohort had a 72.4% response rate and a 12.9-month median duration of response.

The first patient was dosed in TeLuRide-008, a registrational Phase 2/3 trial of EIK1001 with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy for first-line treatment of stage 4 NSCLC. A dose-selection interim analysis is anticipated in the second half of 2027.
ESMO presentations reported clinical activity across EIK1003 and EIK1004, Eikon’s selective PARP1 inhibitor programs, and preliminary findings from its WRN helicase inhibitor EIK1005 program.

Eikon submitted an IND application for EIK1006, a potential next-generation androgen receptor antagonist for advanced metastatic prostate cancer. Subject to FDA clearance, the company plans to begin a Phase 1/2 study.
